title: A point isolated in its fibre is quasi-finite on every affine pair (Stacks 01TH, (2) implies (4))
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ with first projection $p:X_s\to X$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that the unique point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=x$ is isolated in $X_s$, i.e. $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$. Let $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq S$ be open subsets whose open subschemes are affine, $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $R=\mathcal O_S(V)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], such that $x\in U$ and $f(U)\subseteq V$; let $\varphi:R\to A$ be the ring map induced by $f$ and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ the prime ideal corresponding to $x$. Then $\varphi$ is of finite type and $R\to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, (2) implies (4): last paragraph of the proof, lines 3723-3726; finite type of R -> A by Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), line 2673

proof.text: *Finite type.* Since $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$ are affine opens with $f(U)\subseteq V$, the implication (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (Stacks 01T2) gives that the ring map $\varphi:R=\mathcal O_S(V)\to A=\mathcal O_X(U)$ induced by $f$ is of finite type.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, proof, third paragraph, line 3707 ('By Lemma lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize the ring map R -> A is of finite type'); Lemma Tag 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), line 2673

proof.text: *Affine charts and the prime of $s$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] there are canonical open immersions $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ and $\iota_V:\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with images $U$ and $V$; they are $\iota_U=\mathrm{in}_U\circ a$, $\iota_V=\mathrm{in}_V\circ b$ with $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\xrightarrow{\sim}U$, $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ isomorphisms of schemes onto the open subschemes and $\mathrm{in}_U,\mathrm{in}_V$ the inclusions, and the prime $\mathfrak q$ of $x$ satisfies $\iota_U(\mathfrak q)=x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-induced-ring-map-spec-square], $\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=f\circ\iota_U$. Let $f_U:U\to V$ be the restriction of $f$, so $\mathrm{in}_V\circ f_U=f\circ\mathrm{in}_U$. Then $\mathrm{in}_V\circ f_U\circ a=f\circ\iota_U=\iota_V\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=\mathrm{in}_V\circ b\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$, and since a morphism into the open subscheme $V$ is determined by its composite with $\mathrm{in}_V$ (on points $\mathrm{in}_V$ is injective, and on structure sheaves $\mathrm{in}_V^{-1}\mathcal O_S\to\mathcal O_V$ is the identity of $\mathcal O_S|_V$ [def-weil-open-immersion]), $f_U\circ a=b\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$. On points, $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi(\mathfrak q)=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=:\mathfrak p$ and $\iota_V(\mathfrak p)=f(\iota_U(\mathfrak q))=f(x)=s$, so $\mathfrak p$ is the prime of $R$ corresponding to $s$ and $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Put $F=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $j:A\to F$, $a'\mapsto a'\otimes1$, and let $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ be the prime of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$, which exists and is unique by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, proof, third paragraph, lines 3702-3710 (the pair of affine opens, the primes q and p, the fibre ring A tensor kappa(p) and the prime q-bar)

proof.text: *The open piece $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ is the fibre of $f_U$.* Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ with projections $p:X_s\to X$, $\varpi:X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and $c:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ the canonical morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to the open immersion $\mathrm{in}_V$ and the point $s\in V$, the map $r:\kappa_S(s)\to\kappa_V(s)$ on residue fields is an isomorphism and $\mathrm{in}_V\circ j^V_s=c\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)$, where $j^V_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_V(s)\to V$ is the canonical morphism of $V$; so $c_V:=j^V_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)^{-1}:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to V$ satisfies $\mathrm{in}_V\circ c_V=c$, i.e. $c_V$ is the restriction of $c$ to $V\supseteq c(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s))=\{s\}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to $f$, $c$ and the opens $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$: the canonical morphism $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to X_s$, the fibre product taken over $f_U$ and $c_V$, is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] with image $p^{-1}(U)\cap\varpi^{-1}(W)=p^{-1}(U)$, and it carries the first projection to $U$ (followed by $\mathrm{in}_U$) to $p$ restricted to $p^{-1}(U)$. In particular $p^{-1}(U)$ is open in $X_s$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, proof, line 3711 ('Since Spec(A-bar) is an open subscheme of the fibre X_s') and last paragraph, lines 3723-3726 ('U_s ... for any open U')

proof.text: *The fibre of $f_U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F$.* Let $\pi:R\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the canonical map. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] for $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $\mathfrak p$ there is an isomorphism $e:\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $j^{\operatorname{Spec}R}_{\mathfrak p}=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)\circ\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})$; by [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] applied to the isomorphism (in particular open immersion) $b$ and $\mathfrak p\mapsto s$, $b\circ j^{\operatorname{Spec}R}_{\mathfrak p}=j^V_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_b)$ with $r_b:\kappa_V(s)\to\kappa_{\operatorname{Spec}R}(\mathfrak p)$ an isomorphism. Hence $b^{-1}\circ c_V=b^{-1}\circ j^V_s\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)^{-1}=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi)\circ\theta$ with $\theta=\operatorname{Spec}(e^{-1})\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r_b)^{-1}\circ\operatorname{Spec}(r)^{-1}:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ an isomorphism of schemes. Since $f_U\circ a=b\circ\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ (step 2) with $a,b$ isomorphisms, the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] shows that $U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (over $f_U$, $c_V$), with first projection composed with $a^{-1}$ and second projection composed with $\theta$, is a fibre product of $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\pi$: a pair $(t_1:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A,\ t_2:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi\circ t_1=\operatorname{Spec}\pi\circ t_2$ corresponds bijectively to the pair $(a\circ t_1,\theta^{-1}\circ t_2)$ with $f_U\circ a\circ t_1=c_V\circ\theta^{-1}\circ t_2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))=\operatorname{Spec}F$ with first projection $\operatorname{Spec}(j)$. By uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism compatible with the projections [def-pc-fibre-product] and step 3, there is a homeomorphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}F\to p^{-1}(U)$ onto the open subset $p^{-1}(U)$ of $X_s$ with $p\circ h=\iota_U\circ\operatorname{Spec}(j)$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, proof, third paragraph, lines 3708-3711 (the fibre ring A-bar = A tensor_R kappa(p), 'Spec(A-bar) is an open subscheme of the fibre X_s')

proof.text: *$\xi$ is $h(\overline{\mathfrak q})$, and it is isolated in $\operatorname{Spec}F$.* By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $p$ is a homeomorphism of $X_s$ onto the subspace $f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$, and $\xi$ is the point with $p(\xi)=x$. Since $x\in U$, $\xi\in p^{-1}(U)$, so $\xi=h(\mathfrak Q)$ for a prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $F$ (step 4), and $\iota_U(j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q))=\iota_U(\operatorname{Spec}(j)(\mathfrak Q))=p(h(\mathfrak Q))=x=\iota_U(\mathfrak q)$. As $\iota_U$ is an open immersion, it is injective on points [def-weil-open-immersion], so $j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)=\mathfrak q$, and by the injectivity of $\mathfrak Q\mapsto j^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection], $\mathfrak Q=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. By hypothesis $\{\xi\}$ is open in $X_s$; it is contained in $p^{-1}(U)$, hence open in the subspace $p^{-1}(U)$, and as $h$ is a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}F\to p^{-1}(U)$, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}=h^{-1}(\{\xi\})$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$. (This is the source's remark that a point isolated in $X_s$ is isolated in the open $U_s=p^{-1}(U)$.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, proof, last paragraph, lines 3723-3726 ('if x is an isolated point of X_s then it is also an isolated point of U_s for any open U which contains it')

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By step 1, $\varphi$ is of finite type; by step 2, $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$ and $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is the prime of $F=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$; by step 5, $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$. This is the definition of $R\to A$ being quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].
